canonical.object: Finite-Memory Laplacian/Telegraph Generator as the Social-Instability/Peace Spine
canonical.reading: q_D reads the Genesis root operator L_R directly onto a social-tension field: nodes are social units, edges are coupling, dissipation Γ/repair rate corresponds to restorative-justice mechanisms, and sustained load J/S_env corresponds to inequality or humiliation; slow spectral modes of the resulting generator are read as persistent, structurally durable violence/instability, and force-based suppression (acting only on state amplitude) is shown never to change L_R itself.
canonical.canonical_text: L_R = D_W − W (forced Laplacian); A := L_R + Γ; s[n+1] = s[n] + dt(−A s[n] + J). L1 (invariance/recurrence): a bounded amplitude-only intervention cannot move the fixed point s*=A^{-1}J, and the state returns above threshold after a finite computable number of ticks once the intervention ends. L2 (the bill): holding the state at threshold requires a non-vanishing per-tick force, cumulative cost growing linearly in time held. L3 (operator change): raising dissipation γ_i (an operator-level change, not amplitude suppression) can push the fixed point permanently below threshold at zero ongoing force. L4 (mutation): suppressing one node under permanent resets produces a strictly positive long-run floor in a coupled neighbour node.
